This is a huge delta: **90 commits, 409 files, +44k/-3.9k lines**, with **5 new Alembic migrations**. It covers the entire admin-control-centre epic (ADR 0043 workspace membership/RBAC, offboarding, health scoring, orphan-secret sweep), the LLM in-app UI, zero-sample-mode privacy, notification channels, an audit-chain fix, plus the full docs-site redesign — since the last deploy on `6c9588e2` (2026-09-02).

Given the size and that it touches auth/membership/offboarding (security-sensitive) and adds migrations, I want to confirm scope before burning a large QA+deploy effort.

questions.question: This delta is huge (90 commits, 409 files, 5 migrations, spans RBAC/offboarding/LLM UI/docs redesign). How should I scope the QA pass before deploying?

options.label: Full rigorous QA (Recommended)
options.description: Run qa-verifier (CI-mirroring battery + local API/authz probes), ui-tester (desktop+mobile parity), and Playwright E2E against a local stack seeded with the SF PAT, covering all major surfaces touched (admin/RBAC/offboarding, LLM UI, notifications, migrations up/down). Slower but matches the size of this delta.

options.label: Focused on highest-risk areas only
options.description: Skip full UI/mobile sweep; concentrate qa-verifier + targeted Playwright checks on the security-sensitive parts only: RBAC/workspace-membership, offboarding, audit-chain fix, and migration up/down safety. Faster, but leaves LLM UI / notifications / docs less verified.

options.label: Just run CI-equivalent checks + smoke
options.description: Local lint/type/test battery (qa-verifier) plus a basic smoke via Playwright of login + a couple core flows. Fastest, lowest confidence given the delta size.

Environment note: the local Snowflake PAT is expired, which blocked live-data verification of a few flows (noted per-item below, not counted as product defects).

I could not test everything in the prompt to full depth in one pass (self-demotion completion, webhook-secret regen, live LLM output) — reasons given per item. Everything else in the brief was exercised end-to-end against the real running app.

---

### Desktop findings

1. **New — Silent no-feedback path confirmed benign on inspection, not a defect.** Creating a notification channel with an invalid Teams webhook host returned a 422 (`webhook_invalid`, allowed hosts `webhook.office.com`/`logic.azure.com`) and the modal showed no visible error at the time I captured the snapshot. 2. **Known — #605 (still reproduces).** A suite run that fails to execute (expired Snowflake PAT, see below) surfaces only "The run failed to execute. See the server logs for details." in the Run-detail page, even though the worker log (`docker compose logs worker`) carries a fully classifiable reason: `snowflake.connector.errors.DatabaseError: 394401 (08001)… Programmatic access token is expired.` Root cause is upstream of the UI — `backend/app/services/run_service.py:339` catches the datasource exception and the REST/UI layer never surfaces the classified message, exactly the gap #605 tracks.

3. **Known — cosmetic antd v6 deprecation warnings (#1275 class, still reproduces).** Two distinct console warnings observed during the sweep: `antd: List` component deprecated (fires on the Offboard receipt's "Not done, and why" list, `frontend/src/pages/admin/OffboardModal.tsx:252`) and `antd: Table` `rowKey` function's `index` parameter deprecated (fires on the incident-evidence "Metric trend"/"Other checks" tables in the asset page). Cosmetic, no user-facing effect.

4. **Environment limitation, not a code defect — both seeded Snowflake connections have an expired PAT.** `docker compose logs worker` shows `Programmatic access token is expired` for `SF - Retail` and a `SecretNotFoundError` for `SF - Analytics` (`conn-snowflake-sf-analytics-dev-d12d9512` not set in OpenBao). - **Admin → Members**: invite flow (`Add member`) correctly warns "This turns membership enforcement on" before the first member is added, auto-imports the existing signed-in user for review, and the resulting `Confirm`/`Remove` review flow works. 1. **Only rotate credentials through the app's own `POST /connections/{id}/reauth` endpoint** (via the UI or an authenticated API call), never by writing directly into Key Vault / Secrets Manager / OpenBao.
